question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cotangent function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\operatorname{arcoth}⁡({x}^{2}-1)] \\  & =\frac{1}{1-{({x}^{2}-1)}^{2}}\cdot {({x}^{2}-1)}^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{1-({x}^{4}-2{x}^{2}+1)}\cdot 2x \\  & =\frac{2x}{2{x}^{2}-{x}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}(2-{x}^{2})} \\  & =\frac{2}{x(2-{x}^{2})}.\end{aligned}
$$
